draft.title: Using a light microscope
card: A light microscope has an eyepiece lens, which you look through, and several objective lenses on a rotating nose piece. Each lens has its own magnification, such as 10×, 4× or 40×.
Total magnification = eyepiece lens × objective lens. An eyepiece of 10× with an objective of 40× gives 10 × 40 = 400×.
Always start with the lowest power objective lens. It shows the widest view, so the specimen is easier to find and bring into focus.
Then move to a higher power objective to see more detail. Refocus each time you change lens.
draft.remember: Multiply the two lenses for total magnification, and start on low power.

a.q: A student uses a 10× eyepiece lens and a 4× objective lens. What is the total magnification?
a.why: Total magnification is the eyepiece lens times the objective lens, so 10 × 4 = 40×. Adding the numbers to get 14× is the tempting mistake, but the lenses are multiplied.

b.q: Ravi has put a slide of onion cells on the stage. Which step should he do first?
opts: Focus using the lowest power objective lens
Focus using the highest power objective lens
Add the eyepiece and objective numbers together
Swap to the highest power to find the cells quickly
b.why: The lowest power gives the widest view, so the cells are easier to find and focus. Starting on high power is tempting because it shows more detail, but the view is narrow and the specimen is hard to find.
b.clue: Which lens gives the widest view?

b.best: Focus using the lowest power objective lens
